abstract: In this study, we investigate the wCDM dynamical dark energy model with spatial curvature utilizing the recently released DESI Collaboration data (DR1 and DR2) in conjunction with other observational probes such as BBN, Observational Hubble Data (OHD), and Pantheon Plus (PP). Our investigation attempts to discover which DESI dataset gives a better match to the wCDM framework and assess the impact of spatial curvature on cosmological constraints. We find that the cosmic curvature parameter, <math altimg="si1.svg"><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub></math>, disfavors the cosmological constant for the DR2+BBN and DR2+BBN+OHD data combinations. However, the deviation from the cosmological constant remains below the 1σ level, indicating a mild preference for a open universe. In contrast, when using the DR1 based combinations namely DR1+BBN and DR1+BBN+OHD—the deviation from the cosmological constant increases to approximately 1.2σ, suggesting a slightly stronger indication of a open geometry. Also, the best-fit values of the Hubble constant (<math altimg="si2.svg"><msub><mrow><mi>H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></math>) obtained from the DR1+BBN+OHD+PP and DR2+BBN+OHD+PP combinations within the dynamical dark energy model are consistent with the results reported by the Planck Collaboration. Our findings provide constraints on the dark energy EoS parameter <math altimg="si3.svg"><msub><mrow><mi>w</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></math>, reveal a mild but notable deviation from the vacuum energy (<math altimg="si4.svg"><mi>w</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mo><mn>1</mn></math>) scenario at a significance level 1.8σ from DR2+BBN+OHD+PP and 0.5σ from DR1+BBN+OHD+PP, both favoring the quintessence region of dark energy. Furthermore, the key physical distance measures <math altimg="si5.svg"><msub><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi></mrow></msub></math>, <math altimg="si6.svg"><msub><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>V</mi></mrow></msub></math>, and <math altimg="si7.svg"><msub><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi></mrow></msub></math> show better consistency with our model when analyzed with the DR2 data.
title: Constraints on Spatial Curvature and Dark Energy Dynamics in the $w$CDM Model from DESI DR1 and DR2
